title: Full port scan by default + SNMP non-standard port support: cover AutoPenBench NS1 and NS3
goal: AutoPenBench NS1 (SSH on non-standard port) and NS3 (SNMP on non-standard port) fail because: (1) nmap uses --top-ports by default and misses services on non-standard ports. (2) SNMP runner is hard-coded to port 161 (workers/runners/snmp_enum/runner.py line 146). Fix both: (1) Nmap: For active-tier scans, enable full port scan (-p-) by default, or at minimum scan top-10000 ports instead of top-1000. Add a wizard/settings option: 'Scan depth: Top 1000 ports / Top 10000 ports / All 65535 ports'. The full_port_scan flag already exists in nmap/runner.py line 164 but defaults to False — change default for active-tier to scan top-10000. (2) SNMP: Remove hardcoded port 161 from workers/runners/snmp_enum/runner.py line 146. Replace with a configurable port list defaulting to [161] but expandable via engagement settings (e.g. 161, 1161, 1610, 16100). Also: detect SNMP service on any port from nmap results and probe that port.
scope: AutoPenBench NS1 and NS3 fail due to non-standard ports. Code audit: nmap defaults to top-N ports (misses custom ports), SNMP hard-coded to 161. These are trivial config fixes with significant AutoPenBench coverage impact (+2 tasks = +9% in-vitro).
generation_reason: AutoPenBench NS1+NS3 miss non-standard SSH/SNMP ports. Simple config fixes: nmap top-10000 default for active tier, SNMP configurable port.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Only change nmap default port range and SNMP port config. Do not change any other scanner behavior.

success_criteria: Active-tier nmap scans use top-10000 ports by default (not top-1000).
Full port scan (-p-) available as a wizard/settings option.
SNMP runner accepts configurable port list (default: [161]).
SNMP runner probes any port nmap identified as SNMP.
AutoPenBench NS1 (SSH on custom port) detected.
AutoPenBench NS3 (SNMP on custom port) detected.
No regression in existing nmap/SNMP tests.
out_of_scope: Full 65535 port scan as default (too slow)
